title: Tandem Finance - Procurement / MSA & DPA Review
summary: Redwood AE + SE reviewed updated MSA and DPA with Tandem Finance procurement and legal. Main issues: data residency, KMS/HSM integration, SLA penalties, and procurement sign-off timeline. Agreed to push an updated MSA with a narrow changeset, share SOC2 report and KMS integration notes, and run a pilot with Redwood Hosted followed by Dedicated if throughput and privacy requirements prove out.
action_items: Jordan Blake - Send redlined MSA/DPA PDF and one-page summary of key changes - due 2025-06-20
Priya Natarajan - Share technical note on KMS/HSM integration and private deployment network diagram - due 2025-06-22
Kim Ortega - Share SOC 2 Type II report and PenTest summary links - due 2025-06-20
Samir Patel (Tandem) - Confirm internal pricing approver and timeline (legal + finance) - due 2025-06-23
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA & DPA and a one-page change summary
Redwood SE to provide KMS/HSM integration doc and network diagram
Tandem to confirm procurement sign-off timeline and internal approvers
Schedule pilot kickoff call (2-week hosted pilot) after MSA agreement
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Kim Ortega (Redwood CSM), Alex Chen (Tandem Head of Legal), Maria Lopez (Tandem Procurement), Samir Patel (Tandem CTO), Ellen Park (Tandem InfoSec)
Link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/procurement-deck.pdf

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. Uh, quick roll call, we have Priya and Kim from my side —
[00:07] Priya: Hi all.
[00:09] Kim: Hello.
[00:10] Alex: Hi this is Alex.
[00:11] Maria: Maria here.
[00:12] Samir: Samir.
[00:13] Ellen: Ellen.
[00:15] Jordan: Great. The goal today is to walk through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, answer legal and security questions, and agree next steps on pricing approval and onboarding. I'll hand to Alex to confirm any high level priorities.

[00:30] Alex: Yeah thanks Jordan. Main priorities for Tandem are data residency in the EU, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and clear SLA language with remedies. We're hoping the changes are narrow not to re-open negotiation too wide. Also procurement wants pricing clarified — there is an internal approval step that takes about two weeks once legal signs off.

[00:48] Jordan: Makes sense. On residency, our Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem options, but for quick time-to-value we typically run a hosted pilot in our EU region with additional safeguards — DPA controls, encryption at rest, and KMS. Priya, do you want to add the technical bits?

[01:05] Priya: Sure. For the hosted pilot we can enable tenant-level encryption and integrate customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge — we call it the KMS proxy, yes. There's also a Dedicated option if you need isolated GPU pools with stronger tenancy separation. Note: some customers prefer Dedicated for strict residency and compliance.

[01:22] Ellen: Quick question on KMS — is Redwood's integration full HSM-backed customer key support, or is it envelope encryption with customer keys stored in our KMS? We need assurance keys never hit Redwood-managed plaintext.

[01:35] Priya: Good question. It's envelope encryption; customer KMS holds the root key. We perform only ephemeral key wrapping, and the plaintext model cache doesn't persist to disk unencrypted. We'll send the detailed integration doc. Sorry I said KMS proxy earlier, internal name, might show up oddly in the docs.

[01:53] Maria: On the MSA side, there are two items in section 7 that legal flagged — limitation of liability and SLA credits. We can't accept open-ended indemnity. Also procurement would like to see service credits more clearly defined for latency and availability.

[02:10] Jordan: Understood. We've historically pushed for a mutual liability cap tied to fees paid in 12 months, and SLA credits up to a percentage — but we can provide a narrower bucket for enterprise deals. Priya, can you speak to latency SLOs and how we measure them?

[02:27] Priya: Yeah, so we publish per-model latency percentiles in the Console and can include the route-level SLOs. Measurement is via our tracing hooks at the API gateway and within the serving runtime; note that network egress or customer-side processing can affect end-to-end numbers. For Dedicated, we can give tighter tail latency due to reserved GPU pools. One caution is that continuous batching and KV cache behavior can make p99 fluctuate with bursty traffic.

[02:56] Samir: I want to be explicit — our production app requires sub-200ms median for chat flows and p95 under 600ms. That's workable on Redwood Dedicated, correct?

[03:06] Priya: Median sub-200 for short prompts is achievable on Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching configs; p95 under 600 is usually achievable but depends on sequence length and concurrency. We'll commit to working with you on workload profiling during the pilot.

[03:20] Ellen: Are the SLAs prohibitive with penalties? We prefer credits over monetary penalties.

[03:25] Jordan: Credits are the standard. We can structure credits as a percentage of monthly fees for the impacted route. Also, for enterprise contracts we sometimes include an SLA admin review cadence and escalation paths with a named SE.

[03:40] Alex: On DPA, section 3.4 around subprocessors — we need a subprocessor list and a 30-day notice for new ones. Can you provide an updated list?

[03:49] Kim: Yes — we'll share the current subprocessor list. We typically provide a 30-day notice for material changes; for critical subprocessors we can add a separate notification.

[03:58] Maria: Pricing — procurement needs a one pager showing committed vs on-demand costs, how dedicated reserved capacity pricing works, and an example TCO for 6 months. Also any discounting thresholds.

[04:12] Jordan: We'll put together a pricing sheet. As a starting point: hosted per-token bill, reserved Dedicated has monthly commit with discount tiers at 25k, 100k, etc. We'll send an illustrative TCO with assumed QPS and token mix. I'll flag that with finance.

[04:28] Samir: For the pilot we want to start in hosted EU region for two weeks — run a synthetic benchmark and a small production traffic slice. If that passes, we'll move to a Dedicated pool in region. Are there any contract blockers for a pilot?

[04:39] Jordan: We usually can run a short hosted pilot under a simple addendum and the DPA; the MSA can be in parallel. Legal sometimes wants an NDA, but you've already sent a DPA redline so that's helpful. We'll propose a pilot addendum that limits liability and scope.

[04:55] Alex: Regarding audit artifacts — SOC 2, penetration test evidence, and data flow diagrams — we need those for InfoSec review.

[05:02] Kim: We'll share SOC 2 Type II report and a PenTest summary link. Also will include a data flow diagram and KMS integration notes.

[05:12] Ellen: On data retention — the DPA shows logs retained for 90 days; we need a configurable retention option down to 30 days for logs and 0 retention for content unless committed otherwise. Is that supported?

[05:24] Priya: We can configure log retention; content retention is controllable on a per-customer basis. For hosted customers, default retention is 90 but we can set to 30 per contract and we have an option to disable persistent content retention if you opt into Dedicated or Private. We'll make that explicit in the DPA.

[05:44] Maria: Legal redlines — I've put comments in section 10 on indemnities and export controls. We also need a better definition of "confidential information" in the MSA so that training rights can't be implied.

[05:56] Jordan: We can add language that prohibits use of customer data for model training and include a clear carve-out. That's standard for enterprise. Priya, can you confirm we can add a no-training clause?

[06:06] Priya: Yes, we can include a no-model-training clause and technical controls to ensure customer inputs are not used to retrain models used in other customers' deployments. We'll provide the exact wording.

[06:16] Alex: One more on disaster recovery and backup copies. We need RTO/RPO expectations for Dedicated pools. Can you propose numbers?

[06:26] Priya: For Dedicated we typically guarantee 99.9% uptime (SLA varies by commitment) and have cross-zone replication for KV caches, target RTO under 2 hours for service-level incidents; RPO depends on workload and cache config but generally under 15 minutes for persisted state. We'll put proposed numbers in the SLA schedule.

[06:46] Samir: Are there any export control clauses that might block us — we're in fintech, certain crypto ops — I want to be sure nothing unexpected there.

[06:54] Alex: Also, procurement needs vendor onboarding forms — we have a standard security questionnaire (SIG-lite) and procurement vendor questionnaire. Can you complete those?

[07:02] Kim: Yes, we can complete SIG-lite; sometimes it takes a week or so to collate artifacts. We'll prioritize SOC2 and the KMS docs.

[07:10] Jordan: To recap so far: Redwood will send redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2 link, KMS integration doc, subprocessor list, and a pricing TCO one-pager. Tandem will confirm procurement approver and timeline and return any final redlines by next week.

[07:26] Maria: That sounds right. On pricing approvals — our finance lead needs a committed number to include in the coming budget cycle; what is the earliest you can give a firm committed-rate quote for Dedicated?

[07:36] Jordan: If we get a commitment level (QPS and concurrency) we can lock a Dedicated quote within 3 business days after profiling. For the pilot, we can provide an illustrative reserved pricing so finance has a number to work with.

[07:49] Samir: For profiling, can Redwood run a synthetic benchmark of our typical prompt distribution? We'll need to share sample prompts and token characteristics.

[07:58] Priya: Yes, send sample traces and prompts; we'll run both synthetic and a replay test (subject to redaction). We may ask to throttle for safety but otherwise we can mirror your workload.

[08:12] Alex: A couple of small items — we saw one clause that referenced "Redwood Decide" in the MSA, I assume that's a typo for Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Console?

[08:22] Jordan: Sorry, yeah, that's a typo on our side — internal shorthand leaks. We'll correct those artifacts in the redline.

[08:28] Ellen: Encryption in transit — TLS termination points, do you offer customer-managed certs if we require mutual TLS?

[08:36] Priya: We support TLS everywhere; mutual TLS for private endpoints is available with Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted endpoints we support mTLS for VPC peered connections and private link. We'll include the configuration steps.

[08:49] Maria: Are there any additional fees for KMS integration or HSM usage? Procurement needs to know if there are add-on charges.

[08:58] Jordan: Typically KMS usage is billed by KMS provider (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) and Redwood does not markup those charges. There may be an engineering integration fee for bespoke on-prem HSMs; we'll flag any such costs in the pricing sheet.

[09:16] Alex: Timeline check — legal needs to ship final MSA to finance by 2025-06-27 to hit our next board procurement cycle. Are you able to commit to providing the redline before 6/20?

[09:28] Jordan: Yes — we'll aim to deliver redlined MSA/DPA and the required artifacts by 2025-06-20. Priya and Kim will have the tech docs by 6/22.

[09:36] Maria: Great. If we accept the pilot, procurement will need a short pilot addendum — can you share a template?

[09:43] Kim: We'll share a pilot addendum template. It usually includes scope, duration (2 weeks), data handling, and a simple liability cap.

[09:53] Samir: For onboarding, who will be our technical contact? We want a named SE.

[09:58] Jordan: Priya will be your SE, and Kim will handle CSM duties for the onboarding; I'll coordinate internally.

[10:05] Alex: Anything else on legal? If not, we'll plan to review the redlines and get back.

[10:09] Ellen: One last security note — we require the ability to obtain audit logs for all admin activity for 365 days. Is that possible?

[10:17] Priya: Yes, audit logs can be exported; default retention is 90 days but we can extend to 365 for enterprise contracts. We'll include export instructions and where to find logs in the Console.

[10:30] Jordan: Okay, let's summarize next steps and owners. Jordan will send redlined MSA/DPA; Priya sends KMS/HSM and benchmarking plan; Kim sends SOC 2 & pen test links; Tandem confirms approver and timeline. We'll target the pilot kickoff the week after the MSA is agreed.

[10:50] Maria: Thanks everyone.
[10:52] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with email and the doc bundle.
[10:55] Alex: Appreciate it.
[10:57] Kim: Bye all.

Summary of outcomes:
- Redwood to provide redlined MSA/DPA and a one-page change summary by 2025-06-20.
- Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II, PenTest summary, subprocessor list, KMS/HSM integration doc, and a pricing TCO one-pager.
- Tandem to confirm internal pricing approver and procurement timeline; aim to return final redlines by 2025-06-23.
- Pilot plan: 2-week hosted EU pilot, synthetic and replay tests, then potential move to Dedicated pool pending results.

References:
- Procurement deck (link above)
- Example pilot addendum template (to be shared)

Notes on transcription: occasional transcript noise, product name typos ("KMS proxy", "Redwood Decide") and filler words preserved.
questions: Can Redwood add a no-training clause to the MSA?
Can audit logs be retained and exported for 365 days?
Is customer-managed KMS/HSM supported without Redwood-accessible plaintext?
What SLA RTO/RPO numbers can Redwood commit to for Dedicated?
